direction: Unfolding, making and distance: fresh colour in a peeled husk, a tentative carpenter’s joint, and a glass carrying the small movement of the sea. Gouache, charcoal and watercolor create three materially different pauses. This is a new reading interpretation, not a claim about the historical issue theme.

items.title: The husk opens
items.rationale: The September poem welcomes seasonal renewal through the comparison of laughing branches to corn kernels revealed by a peeled husk. Choose that modest joyful material moment within this October issue; do not claim an October-specific harvest or illustrate every festival.

review.notes: Normal-size review: pale silk and flexible peeled leaves frame a curved cob with varied kernel rows; contact shadow follows the supported ear. Bright kernel highlights remain small and physically plausible, while matte green strokes and open paper keep the material study painterly. Warm fresh colour supports the poem’s laughing renewal without adding a festival montage or literal seasonal claim. No text, invented people or unrelated props.

items.alt: A partly peeled green maize husk reveals warm yellow kernels against open ivory paper.

items.title: Begin again at the bench
items.rationale: Writing becomes the humble, repeated responsibility of a carpenter shaping uncertain parts. Show an unfinished ordinary joint and space for work to resume; retain hesitation rather than displaying a completed masterpiece or assembling every tool in the poem.

review.notes: Normal-size review: two supported wood pieces present a loose tenon and a facing rectangular mortise, with consistent grain and cut ends. Chisel rests flat and two shavings provide scale without an arranged tool collection. Contact shadows and ordinary diffuse light are coherent. Charcoal/ochre texture is denser near cut surfaces and fades into open bench space; the incomplete fit supports the poem’s careful repeated making rather than a finished trophy.

items.alt: An unfinished wooden mortise-and-tenon joint rests on a bench beside a chisel and two shavings.

items.title: Between sea and thought
items.rationale: The mariner’s distance from the muse briefly contracts around a glass of water trembling on a table, then the ship goes on. Hold that ordinary ripple and the sea beyond; do not fabricate a real voyage, beloved person or dramatic dolphin encounter.

review.notes: Concentric rings are too regular and strong, and a second nested ring cluster beneath the waterline reads as a floating diagram. Simplify only the water ripple/refraction; preserve composition.

Source/v2 comparison at normal size: correction substantially softens the concentric marks and the submerged-looking cluster into faint surface movement and reflection. Several traces remain but no longer dominate as a diagram at reading size. Glass ellipses, halfway water level, base contact and coherent rail/horizon stay intact. Soft sea/wood washes preserve literary distance and intimacy without an invented voyage or person. Selected v2; v1 retained.

items.alt: A half-full glass with faint ripples rests on a dark table aboard a ship, with pale sea and sky beyond a simple rail.

text_led.rationale: Five haiku each make a distinct small encounter; one picture would privilege one poem and a collage would flatten the pauses. Preserve all five in a text-led opening.
The father/daughter reversals carry the grief and medical identity. Avoid invented family likenesses, certificates or a staged hospital scene.
The poem questions easy patriotism through a refugee child and maternal grief. Keep its witness in language without invented documentary victim imagery.
